inventory.editFamilyHelp: Changes {count, plural, one {this model} other {all # variants}} at once: name, manufacturer, category and flags. Sizes, stock, weights and prices stay per variant.
inventory.labelsHelp: {count, plural, one {One label} other {# labels}} with the QR code, asset tag and model, as a PDF to print.

inventory.newModelFromWish: New model from the wish list
inventory.colorsHelp: Colours are set on top-level categories and show as a bar in lists, on the model page, in the gear picker and on packing lists. Screen only, never printed.

inventory.minStockHelp: Shown on the dashboard when stock drops below this.

settings.title: Settings
settings.usersHelp: Who can sign in and what they may do.

settings.name: Name
settings.roleHelp: Admin: everything incl. users. Member: edit gear, projects, lists, plans. Viewer: read-only.
settings.googleEmailHelp: Used to invite the user to calendar events.
settings.passwordHelp: At least 8 characters. Share it with the user; they can change it under Settings › Your account.
settings.apiTokensHelp: Use a token as a Bearer header to call the REST API from other tools. Docs at /api/docs.
settings.tokenCreated: Token created. Copy it now; it will not be shown again.
settings.cfKeyHelp: Lowercase identifier used in exports and the API, e.g. lamp_hours. Cannot change later.
settings.noCustomFieldsBody: Extra fields appear on the entity's forms, pages, filters and exports.
settings.deleteFieldConfirm: Delete this field? Existing values stay in the database but are no longer shown.
settings.webhooksHelp: Send a signed POST to your own URL when something happens.
settings.calendarHelp: Feed links and Google Calendar push.
settings.webhookSecretHelp: Used to sign the body: X-Vertigo-Signature: sha256=HMAC(secret, body).
settings.webhookEventsHelp: Leave all unchecked to receive every event.
settings.noWebhooksBody: Webhooks let other tools react to changes without code changes here.
settings.outboxHelp: Webhook deliveries and calendar syncs waiting, done or failed.
settings.contactsHelp: People and companies who are not users: borrowers, suppliers, partners, key-fob holders.
settings.cfCategoryHelp: Only models or items in this category (and its sub-categories) get the field. Leave empty for all.
settings.importHelp: Load the gear spreadsheet: preview what will be created, decide the doubtful rows, then confirm.
settings.pricingHelp: Rate tables (days → factor) used to price quotes and rental agreements.
settings.backupHelp: Download the whole database as a file, or restore one (admins).
settings.twoFactorHelp: Besides your password, sign-in asks for a code from an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password …).
settings.twoFactorOn: On since {since}. {count, plural, =0 {No recovery codes left: make new ones.} one {# recovery code left.} other {# recovery codes left.}}
settings.twoFactorRequired: Your role requires two-factor sign-in, so it cannot be turned off. If you lose your phone, use a recovery code or ask an admin to reset it.
settings.recoveryCodesHelp: Each one signs you in once without the app. Store them somewhere safe (a password manager, or printed); they are shown only now. Older codes no longer work.
settings.twoFactorOnFor: Two-factor sign-in is on for this user.
settings.twoFactorOffFor: Two-factor sign-in is off for this user.
settings.twoFactorResetConfirm: Reset two-factor sign-in for {name}? They sign in with the password alone and set it up again (required for admins).
settings.searchWordsHelp: Words that mean the same in a search: arbejdslys finds worklight.
settings.glossaryIntro: One group per line, words separated by commas. A search for any word in a group also finds the others, in the inventory, the items, the packing-list gear picker and the apps. Names are never changed. Spaces and capitals do not matter, so “work light” and “worklight” are the same word. Groups do not chain: a word in two lines gets both lines, but not what those lines link to.
settings.glossarySaved: Saved {count, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}}.
settings.layoutHelp: Roomy pages with columns, or the compact layout, for everyone.
settings.layoutIntro: How busy pages use a wide screen. It applies to everyone; phones always show one column.
settings.layout_roomyHelp: Busy pages use more of a wide screen: the packing list in two or three columns, schedule and tasks side by side on the production plan, the project page in two columns, and pack mode and check-in with their lines in columns.
settings.layout_compactHelp: Every page keeps the narrower width and shows one column, as before.
settings.layoutSaved: Saved. Every page now uses this layout.

rentals.noLines: No gear on this rental yet.

rentals.markOutConfirm: Hand the gear out? Assigned units move to the renter.
rentals.markReturnedConfirm: Mark everything returned? Assigned units go back to their home location.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.subtitle: Projects and rentals on a timeline. Red marks days where a model is over-booked.
calendar.feedsHelp: Subscribe to these in Google Calendar (Other calendars › From URL) or Apple Calendar. Anyone with the link can read the feed; rotate it if it leaks.
calendar.rotateConfirm: Rotate this link? Calendars using the old link stop updating.
calendar.googleOn: Configured. Confirmed projects and rentals are pushed to the shared calendars.
calendar.googleOff: Not configured. Set GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON and GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID_PROJECTS (see README).
calendar.jobEventsHelp: Each job is one all-day event over its whole span, with every phase in the description. Build-up and pack-down are timed events from their call time (one per day), and the show from its start to its end. A build-up or pack-down without a call time only shows in the all-day event.
calendar.callHoursHelp: From the call time, in half hours. Saving updates every job in Google Calendar; subscribed feeds follow on their next refresh.
calendar.callHoursSaved: Saved: {hours} h. Every job is being updated in Google Calendar.

importer.title: Import spreadsheet
importer.subtitle: The Vertigo gear list (.xlsx). Nothing is written until you confirm the preview.
importer.fileHelp: Vertigo Gearliste _ Status.xlsx or a newer export with the same sheets.
importer.how1: Every sheet is read: cables, LED, controllers, projectors, computers, truss, stands, rods, loans, key fobs.
importer.how2: The preview sorts rows into: will import, imported with an assumption (shown), needs a decision (you choose), and parked (kept for a later feature; nothing on the current sheet).
importer.how3: Rows for models or tags that already exist are skipped unless you say otherwise, so re-running an export is safe.
importer.how4: Every imported model, unit, contact and location remembers its cell (Sheet!A1).
importer.previewSubtitle: {rows} rows read. Check the decisions and assumptions, then confirm.
importer.bucket_parked_help: belongs to a feature that is not built yet; shown, not written

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.subtitle: Rate tables turn a model's day price into a price for the whole period: price × factor(days) × quantity.
pricing.noTablesBody: Create one, or run the seed to get Standard, Theatre and Revised from the spreadsheet.
pricing.howItWorks: Days between tiers use the nearest lower tier. Beyond the last tier the table's rule adds a factor per further day or per started 10 days. Every quote picks a table (the default unless chosen) and can override the number of charge days.
pricing.isDefaultHelp: Used by projects and rentals that have not chosen a table.
pricing.tiersHelp: Number of days and the factor the day price is multiplied by. Missing days use the nearest lower tier.
pricing.extraRuleHelp: What happens for longer periods than the last tier.
pricing.deleteConfirm: Delete this rate table? Projects and rentals using it fall back to the default.
pricing.settingsHelp: Which rate table, how many days are charged, and a discount on the whole document.
pricing.noRateTable: No rate table exists yet; everything is priced at factor 1. Create one under
pricing.chargeDaysHelp: Leave empty to charge the {days} days of the period.
pricing.chargeDaysValue: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} charged
pricing.termsHelp: Shown on the PDF. Leave empty for the default text.
pricing.defaultTerms: All prices excl. VAT, freight and insurance.
pricing.agreementTerms: The renter is responsible for the equipment from hand-over until return and for any loss or damage at replacement value. Equipment is returned clean and complete, in the same cases, at the agreed date.
pricing.extraLineHelp: A fixed amount that is not multiplied by the rate factor: freight, insurance, crew, consumables.
pricing.empty: Nothing to price yet: reserve gear or add a line.
pricing.gearLinesSummary: {count, plural, one {# gear line} other {# gear lines}} (above)
pricing.projectQuoteHelp: Gear lines come from the reservations; use {edit} on a reservation to change its day price or discount.

backup.title: Backup
backup.subtitle: The database as one JSON file: every table, every row. Uploaded files are not inside; scripts/backup.sh on the server takes both.
backup.downloadHelp: Every row of all {tables} tables, with ids, so a restore puts everything back exactly. Keep the file somewhere safe: it holds client details and password hashes.
backup.filesNote: Photos, drawings and 3D files live on the uploads volume. On the server, scripts/backup.sh bundles the database and the uploads into one archive every night.
backup.restoreWarning: Restoring replaces everything in the database with the file's contents. There is no undo. Download a backup first.
backup.restored: Restored {rows} rows in {tables} tables. Reload the app.

specImport.title: Import specs
specImport.subtitle: Fill in weight, size, power draw, description, links, lumen and throw ratio on existing models from a sheet. Nothing is written until you confirm.
specImport.fileHelp: Semicolons or commas, one row per model, with the Id column from Inventory › Export CSV.
specImport.errors: Fix these rows in the sheet first:
specImport.summaryFill: {count, plural, one {# empty field} other {# empty fields}} to fill in
specImport.summaryKeep: {count, plural, one {# value differs} other {# values differ}} from the model
specImport.summaryUnknown: {count, plural, one {# unknown id} other {# unknown ids}}
specImport.apply: Save {fields, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}} on {models, plural, one {# model} other {# models}}
specImport.explain: Ticked changes are saved. Empty fields start ticked. Where the model already has a different value, it starts unticked and stays; tick it to use the sheet's value instead. Links are added when they are new. Every model in the sheet is marked as checked (only in the CSV export), so a later lookup can skip it; leave a model out of the sheet to have it looked up again.
specImport.showAll: Also show models where nothing changes
specImport.unknown: No model has the id on row {lines}. It may have been deleted since the export.
specImport.done: Done: {fields, plural, one {# change} other {# changes}} saved on {models, plural, one {# model} other {# models}}, and {checked, plural, one {# model} other {# models}} marked as checked. Each model's history says what came from the sheet.
specImport.how1: Start from Inventory › Export CSV, which gives each model's Id.
specImport.how2: Columns: Id, Weight (kg), Width (cm), Height (cm), Depth (cm), Power (W), Lumen, Throw ratio, Description, Links. Other columns (sources, notes) are ignored. Leave a cell empty to leave the field alone.
specImport.how3: Description: one spec per line ("Max height: 366 cm"). Links: one per line, "Label | https://…".

specImport.unavailableHelp: Some values were skipped because the model's category has no extra field for them (lumen on a category without a Lumen field, for example). Add the field under Settings › Extra fields, then read the sheet again.
